title: Nvidia's NOOA Framework Shows the AI Harness, Not the Model, Is What Drives Performance
excerpt: An open-source Python framework from Nvidia Labs achieves top benchmark scores at half the token cost of competing systems, suggesting that how you orchestrate an AI model matters as much as the model itself.
body:
• Nvidia Labs open-sourced NOOA (NVIDIA Object-Oriented Agents), a Python framework that turns AI agents into standard Python classes — with methods as actions, fields as state, and docstrings as prompts — and achieved 82.2% on SWE-bench Verified and 86.8% on CyberGym L1 at roughly half the token cost of competing open harnesses.
  • On ARC-AGI-3, a single NOOA agent with a one-page world-model skill reached 85.1% mean RHAE using GPT-5.6-sol at under $20 per game, suggesting the orchestration layer is a bigger performance lever than the model alone.
  • The framework uses a pass-by-reference design that keeps large data objects live in a Python REPL rather than pasting them into context, eliminating the need for context compaction on benchmarks like SWE-bench.
  • NOOA is released as alpha software under Apache 2.0 and requires OS-level isolation for safe deployment, as agents can execute LLM-generated code directly.

An Agent as a Python Object

Nvidia Labs released NOOA — NVIDIA Object-Oriented Agents — on July 30, a model-agnostic Python framework that collapses the scattered components of AI agent development into a single class. In a conventional agent stack, developers manage a patchwork of prompt templates, tool schemas, callback code, and workflow graphs, each with its own interface. NOOA replaces all of that with standard Python: methods become the actions a model can take, fields hold agent state, docstrings serve as prompts, and type annotations are contracts that the runtime enforces.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=b-o5vcOAV9o

A method whose body is Python's ellipsis literal — ... — becomes an "agentic method" completed at runtime by an LLM-driven loop. A method with a normal body stays deterministic Python the model can call as a tool. Developers and models share one interface, which means agent behavior can be tested, traced, refactored, and version-controlled like any other software.

The Benchmark Results

The performance numbers are striking, but the efficiency story is the headline. A benchmark-agnostic 253-line agent running NOOA with GPT-5.5 reached 82.2% on SWE-bench Verified — a widely used measure of automated software engineering — compared to 78.6% for OpenCode and 78.2% for PI, a competing open harness. With Opus 4.6, the same setup scored 79.8%.

That 82.2% came at roughly 1.1 million tokens and about 28 model calls per task. PI, by comparison, required approximately 2.2 million tokens and 66 calls to reach its lower score. Nvidia attributes part of the efficiency gap to validated termination: OpenCode stops when the model replies without making a tool call, while NOOA requires the agent to submit a typed TaskResult object with supporting evidence and a verification command — a small design choice that appears to prevent wasted turns.

"Agent development today is split across prompt templates, tool schemas, callback code, and workflow graphs. NOOA collapses all of it into one Python class."

— Nvidia Labs, NOOA Technical Blog

Beyond Software Engineering

On CyberGym L1, a cybersecurity benchmark run with network access blocked, NOOA solved 86.8% of tasks — the strongest open-source result reported on the benchmark, according to Nvidia. On Terminal-Bench 2.0, it scored 73.0% at high effort, though PI leads at extra-high effort with 75.3%.

The ARC-AGI-3 results are particularly telling. ARC-AGI-3 tests general reasoning with abstract pattern-recognition tasks that even frontier AI models struggle with, though every task has been solved by human participants. A single NOOA agent equipped with just a one-page world-model skill reached a mean relative human-adjusted efficiency of 50.2% with GPT-5.5 and 85.1% with GPT-5.6-sol, all at under $20 per game played. The gap between models using the same harness underscores that the model still matters — but the harness determines how efficiently that model's capability is deployed.

Six Ideas, One Surface

Nvidia's research team identified six model-facing capabilities it claims to be the first framework to combine: typed input/output, pass by reference over live objects, code as action, programmable loop engineering, explicit object state, and model-callable harness APIs. The team scored 14 existing frameworks and harnesses — including LangGraph, Google ADK, PydanticAI, smolagents, Claude Agent SDK, and OpenAI Codex — and reports only partial coverage in each.

Pass by reference is the load-bearing innovation. Arguments arrive as live Python objects; the model sees only a bounded preview with the type, length, and a head/tail sample. A 100-element list renders in about 30 tokens while the full variable stays in the REPL. Context is split into a cacheable static prefix, an append-only typed event history, and dynamic blocks at the tail, preserving KV-cache reuse across turns.

"NOOA hit 82.2% on SWE-bench Verified using roughly 1.1 million tokens and about 28 model calls per task. PI needed about 2.2 million tokens and 66 calls to reach a lower 78.2%."

— CodeMagnet analysis of NOOA benchmarks

What It Means for the Industry

NOOA ships under Apache 2.0 and installs with pip, but Nvidia classifies it as a research preview. Because agents can execute LLM-generated code directly, the framework's built-in AST checks and module deny-lists are defense-in-depth guardrails, not a containment boundary. Nvidia recommends deploying inside a container, virtual machine, or its own OpenShell sandbox.

The broader takeaway is architectural. As AI models converge in capability, the orchestration layer — how you structure the loop, manage context, and validate outputs — is emerging as the differentiator. Nvidia's results suggest that a well-designed harness can extract meaningfully better performance from the same model at half the cost, a message with direct implications for companies building AI-powered products and the engineers designing them.
nri_angle: Indian engineers and AI researchers in the diaspora — who form a significant share of the global AI workforce — will find NOOA relevant as an open-source tool for building more efficient AI agent systems.
